hz1_lebanon.topic: Lebanon's confessional system, the Shia, Musa al-Sadr and Amal

claims.text: The National Pact of 1943 was an unwritten arrangement between President Bechara el-Khoury and PM Riad al-Solh, made public 7 Oct 1943: Maronite president, Sunni PM, Shia speaker, Greek Orthodox deputy speaker; 6:5 Christian-to-Muslim ratio based on the 1932 census; Taif (1989) moved parliament to 50:50.

LoC country study: the Pact distributed high posts by confession on the 1932 census, 6:5 favouring Christians; Muslims accepted the 1920 borders and renounced union with Syria, Christians renounced French protection and accepted Lebanon's 'Arab face'; it 'merely perpetuated the power of the privileged'.
MRG: before the 1960s most Shia 'remained on the political and economic periphery'; by 1975, 40% of Jabal Amel's Shia had moved to Beirut; Shia up to 32% of population but 21% of seats.

Musa al-Sadr, born Qom 1928, arrived in Tyre late 1959; first head of the Supreme Islamic Shia Council 1969; founded the Movement of the Deprived 1974 with Hussein el-Husseini; schools and clinics in the south.
Britannica: Amal formed 1975 as armed wing of Harakat al-Mahrumin to defend the Shia community in the civil war; community 'largely disenfranchised'.

Sadr went to Libya 25 Aug 1978 with Sheikh Mohammad Yaacoub and journalist Abbas Badreddine; last seen 31 Aug 1978; Libya said they left on Alitalia flight to Rome; Italian authorities concluded in July 2015 he never entered Italy.
Lebanon indicted Gaddafi on 27 Aug 2008; Libya consistently denied responsibility.
Hannibal Gaddafi, seized Dec 2015 and detained in Lebanon for withholding information on the Sadr case, never tried, released on $900,000 bail in Nov 2025.

hz1_plo.topic: Refugees, the Cairo Agreement, the PLO in Lebanon, raids and reprisals, civil war

claims.text: Camps had an estimated 100,000 people when Palestinians first arrived; 452,669 registered in Jan 2015 (true number likely lower); barred from most professions and from owning property.

Cairo Agreement, 3 Nov 1969, signed by Emile Bustani and Yasser Arafat with Egyptian mediation: Palestinians in Lebanon may join the revolution 'through armed struggle'; commandos given passage points and right of passage to Arqub; camps' arms controlled by Armed Struggle posts; clause 15: 'This agreement shall remain top secret.'
Agreement published unofficially by An-Nahar on 20 April 1970; 16 camps (~300,000) moved from Deuxième Bureau jurisdiction to the PLO Armed Struggle Command; annulled by parliament 21 May 1987.
Background: fedayeen attacks on Israel from south Lebanon, Israeli airstrikes and raids, army-fedayeen clashes; President Charles Helou asked Nasser to broker the deal.

Black September: Jordanian army offensive 17 Sept 1970, Cairo ceasefire 27 Sept; Jordan said ~3,000 killed, PLO said tens of thousands; July 1971 Wasfi al-Tel drove Arafat and fighters out, who went to Lebanon.
Other estimates of Palestinians killed in Black September 2,000-3,400; Arafat claimed 25,000; final Ajloun offensive ended July 1971.
UNSCR 262 (31 Dec 1968), adopted unanimously, condemned Israel 'for its premeditated military action' and said Lebanon is entitled to redress.
Israeli commandos (64, led by Rafael Eitan) raided Beirut airport overnight 28 Dec 1968 destroying 12 MEA aircraft, over an attack on an Israeli airliner by the Beirut-based PFLP.
Kiryat Shmona 11 April 1974: three gunmen from Lebanon killed 18 Israelis incl. 8 children; Israel raided south Lebanese villages 13 April.
Ma'alot 15 May 1974: DFLP militants from Lebanon; 25 hostages killed including 22 children.

Civil war began 13 April 1975: after a shooting at an Ain el-Rummaneh church, Phalangists killed about 30 Palestinians on a bus; Syrian troops (~12,000) entered 1 June 1976; ~120,000 died in the whole war.
Aug 1977: Dayan told the US Israel wanted to help southern Lebanese Christians 'in a military way'; Begin publicly admitted Israel had aided them with artillery fire from inside Israel.

hz1_1978.topic: Operation Litani, UNSCR 425/426, Haddad and Free Lebanon, Iran 1979

claims.text: Coastal Road attack 11 March 1978: attackers left Lebanon by boat, landed near Ma'agan Michael; 38 civilians including 13 children killed (figures vary; 71-76 wounded); PLO/Fatah claimed it.

Israel invaded on the night of 14/15 March 1978 and within days occupied the south except Tyre; on 15 March Lebanon told the Security Council it had no connection with the commando operation; UNSCR 425 and 426 adopted 19 March called for Israel to cease action and withdraw and created UNIFIL to confirm withdrawal, restore peace and security, and assist the Lebanese government; first troops arrived 23 March.

Operation Litani: ~25,000 IDF troops; Lebanese and Palestinian dead estimated 1,100 (Norton) to ~2,000 (other sources); Israeli dead 18-20; 100,000-250,000 displaced (other estimates higher); Israel handed positions to Haddad's militia on withdrawal.
Carter to Begin, 24 Sept 1977: 'current Israeli military actions in Lebanon are a violation of our agreements'; warned Congress would be informed and deliveries ended.

Aug 1979: Vance said Israel 'may have violated its agreement' with US by using American weapons in south Lebanon; Israeli military sources said Israel had admitted violating the agreement with cluster bombs in the Litani operation; Israeli defence circles denied violating any agreement otherwise.

Haddad, a Greek Catholic major commanding a ~700-man battalion at Marjayoun, joined a breakaway army force in 1976; proclaimed 'State of Free Lebanon' from Metulla in April 1979; militia mainly Christian but also Shia and Druze; Lahad took over in April 1984 after Haddad's death on 15 Jan 1984; SLA collapsed May 2000.
Free Lebanon proclaimed 18 April 1979; next day Lebanese government branded Haddad a traitor and dismissed him; Good Fence from 1976, work in Israel from 1977, Fatima Gate crossing.
Haddad (1982) said Israel contributed about $10 million to salaries since 1978, $100 a month per man, and provided weapons and services.
April 1981: senior Israeli military sources admitted supplying equipment to Christians in northern Lebanon; Begin spoke of a 'moral commitment'; Israel gave full backing to Haddad's militia.
Alhurra (2026): Good Fence launched 1976 offered medical and economic services to border villages; Israel gave Haddad full financial and military support, about $35 million a year.
Arafat visited Tehran 17 Feb 1979, first official visitor after the revolution; Iran closed the Israeli embassy and handed it to the PLO.
Iran's constitution (adopted Oct 1979) preamble: provides basis for 'the continuation of the Revolution at home and abroad'; armed forces have 'the ideological mission of jihad in God's way'.

Khomeini's New Year message, Radio Tehran 21 March 1980: 'We should try hard to export our revolution to the world'; named 'America, Israel and Zionism'; support for 'beloved Palestine and beloved Lebanon'.
